## Pour Decisions: Alcohol Privatization and Birth Outcomes

Washington's Initiative 1183 substantially expanded spirits access through grocery and big-box stores. I study how that change affected birth outcomes and what the results imply for alcohol-tax design aimed at limiting health harms.

<div class="paper-status">Working paper · Available upon request</div>

![Percent-change estimates for live-birth health outcomes](images/research/pour-decisions.png){.job-market-figure}

<p class="paper-abstract"><strong>Abstract.</strong> Washington's Initiative 1183 privatized spirits retail in June 2012. Using Nielsen Homescan data, restricted-use natality records, and repeated-cross-section synthetic difference-in-differences, I estimate that privatization increased projected household spirits purchases by 35 percent, reduced average birth weight, and increased low-birth-weight and small-for-gestational-age births. Distributional estimates place the response around clinically meaningful lower birth-weight bins.</p>
:::
